memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The person to be cleansed must wash their clothes, shave off all their hair and bathe with water; then they will be ceremonially clean. After this they may come into the camp, but they must stay outside their tent for seven days." - Lev 14:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pronounced clean. Allowed back into the camp. And still, for seven days, not yet back in their own tent.

That is a strange in-between, and many believers know it well. You are forgiven — genuinely, completely — and yet the effects of what happened have not all cleared. The marriage is reconciled but the trust is still being rebuilt. The addiction is broken but the friendships take time to repair. You know God has restored you, and you are still finding your way back to normal life.

Do not read that gap as evidence that God's forgiveness was partial. This person is called clean in the same verse that keeps them outside the tent for a week. Both are true at once.

Forgiveness is instant. Restoration is often a process. God removes our guilt in a moment and then walks with us through the slow work of rebuilding what sin damaged.

Be patient with that process — in yourself and in others. He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6). The waiting week is not exile. It is part of coming home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you confusing slow restoration with incomplete forgiveness?
2. What in your life is still being rebuilt even though God has forgiven you?
3. How can you be patient with someone else's slow road back?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your forgiveness is complete even when my healing is slow. Give me patience for the rebuilding, and confidence that You will finish what You started. Amen.
